core_obligations: Recall that the constant sheaf on an irreducible space has value Z on every nonempty open, and dispose of the zero subsheaf with d = 0 (proof lines 3645-3648).

If the subsheaf is nonzero, choose a nonempty open U with nonzero sections and write them as the multiples of a positive integer n, so that the constant multiples of n sit inside the subsheaf over U (proof lines 3649-3655).

If that inclusion is strict, shrink to a smaller nonempty open and find a strictly smaller positive integer with the same property; the process is well founded, so it terminates and yields the required nonempty open and integer (proof lines 3655-3662).
proof_roadmap: Constant values and the zero case (proof lines 3645-3648).
A nonzero open and its generator (proof lines 3649-3655).
Well-founded descent on the generator (proof lines 3655-3662).
difficulty_reason: On an irreducible topological space X, the lemma shows that any abelian subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z agrees on some nonempty open with the constant sheaf of multiples of a fixed integer (statement lines 3634-3642). The proof uses that the constant sheaf has value Z on every nonempty open, disposes of the zero subsheaf, and then runs a descending induction on the positive generator n of the group of sections over a nonempty open on which the subsheaf is nonzero: if the inclusion of the constant multiples of n is strict, one can shrink and produce a strictly smaller positive integer, and the process must stop (proof lines 3644-3662). The claim is H2: one point of the definition of the constant sheaf on an irreducible space plus a well-founded descent on positive integers, with the shrinking step written out.
